source_name: ARBK — Agjencia e Regjistrimit të Bizneseve në Kosovë (Kosovo Business Registration Agency)
why_relevant: Corporate registry giving legal identity, business number, ownership and status for every licensed financial institution and its agents. Essential for resolving CBK register names to legal entities and for spotting agents/subsidiaries of PSPs that never appear in the CBK list.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore për emetimin e parasë elektronike (E-money issuance regulation, sq/en)
why_relevant: States the CBK obligation to publish a register of licensed/registered electronic money issuers and sets the conditions and deadlines for that licence class — the legal hook for the e-money slice of the register.

source_name: Council of Europe PECK project reports on Kosovo (economic crime / AML supervision assessment)
why_relevant: Independent external assessment of how Kosovo authorities including CBK exercise AML/CFT supervision and sanctioning — reveals enforcement practice and weaknesses that CBK's own publications understate, and names the supervisory instruments actually used.

source_name: Kosovo financial-press coverage of CBK supervisory and licensing decisions (Telegrafi, Koha, Kosova.info, Epoka e Re)
why_relevant: Local media routinely report CBK annual-report approvals, licence actions and consumer-complaint handling before or instead of a dedicated CBK enforcement page; tag pages give a low-cost, crawlable early-warning feed on supervision events.

source_name: ZAKON BR. 08/L-304 O BANKAMA — Serbian-language gazetted text
why_relevant: Serbian is an official language of Kosovo and gazette texts are published in it; the Serbian version is the practical reading route for Serb-community institutions and for cross-checking translation of deadline clauses ('stupanje na snagu'). Also the anchor for Serbian-language query expansion in this cell.

source_name: Kuvendi i Kosovës — English draft-laws register (Draft Laws and Laws)
why_relevant: English mirror of the bill register, useful for entity resolution and for producing English titles of banking/payments bills without machine translation. Alternate mirror hosts exist (assembly-kosova.org, assemblyofkosovo.org) which may be less bot-defended.

source_name: Kuvendi i Kosovës — Zakoni / Predlozi zakona (Serbian-language legislative register)
why_relevant: Serbian-language view of the same bill and law register, satisfying the mandatory sr coverage for the primary-legislation channel and providing the sr title strings ('predlog zakona', 'zakon o ...') needed for query expansion and deduplication.

source_name: Kuvendi i Kosovës — Seancat (plenary sessions: agendas, order of business, records)
why_relevant: Plenary agendas ('rendi i ditës') and session records are where first- and second-reading votes on banking/payments bills actually appear with dates. The Presidency sets the order of business at least three days before a sitting, giving a short but real lead indicator that a bill is about to be voted.

source_name: Kuvendi i Kosovës — Komisioni për Ekonomi, Industri, Ndërmarrësi dhe Tregti
why_relevant: Functional committee that reviews economic/financial-sector bills between the two readings and issues the 'raport me amendamente' — the document that reveals what actually changed in a banking or payments bill before it becomes gazetted law. Committee meeting notices give the earliest concrete signal of amendment direction.

source_name: Kuvendi i Kosovës — Komisioni për Buxhet, Punë dhe Transfere
why_relevant: Budget/finance committee; the alternative or co-reporting committee for finance-sector bills (CBK law, AML/CFT, deposit insurance, financial-agreement ratifications). Determines which committee a banking bill is referred to, which changes where its amendment report will appear.

source_name: Presidentja e Republikës së Kosovës — dekretet e shpalljes së ligjeve (promulgation decrees)
why_relevant: Constitutionally, a law passed by the Assembly must be decreed/promulgated by the President before gazette publication. The presidency's decree announcements are the last checkpoint between an Assembly vote and the gazette entry, and they name the laws promulgated — a reliable few-days-ahead signal of an imminent gazette publication and therefore of the deadline clock starting.

source_name: GZK — LIGJI NR. 03/L-209 për Bankën Qendrore të Republikës së Kosovës (CBK statute record)
why_relevant: The enabling statute cited as legal basis in essentially every CBK regulation ('Bazuar në nenin 35/36 ... të Ligjit nr. 03/L-209'). Any amendment to it changes the CBK's rule-making authority and therefore the whole downstream regulation stack — a high-leverage statute to watch in the Assembly pipeline.

source_name: GZK — LIGJI NR. 05/L-096 për Parandalimin e Pastrimit të Parave dhe Luftimin e Financimit të Terrorizmit
why_relevant: The AML/CFT statute (voted in plenary 25 May 2016, gazetted June 2016) that drives customer due-diligence and reporting obligations for banks, payment institutions and the FIU. AML statutes in Kosovo are amended repeatedly under EU-alignment and MONEYVAL pressure, so this act page is a recurring deadline generator. Predecessor act 03/L-196 also on GZK, useful for lineage.

source_name: assembly-kosova.org / assemblyofkosovo.org — Assembly mirror domains
why_relevant: Alternate hostnames serving the same Assembly CMS (calendar, committee pages, per-bill 'draftlawopen' pages). Valuable as a fallback collection route when the primary kuvendikosoves.org host blocks automated fetches, and as a source of the alternative per-bill URL pattern /projektligjet-dhe-ligjet/draftlawopen/?draftlaw=NNN.

source_name: old.kuvendikosoves.org — legacy Assembly document archive
why_relevant: Legacy Assembly site retaining documents from earlier legislatures (pre-redesign). Needed for reconstructing the legislative history of older banking statutes (04/L-093, 04/L-155, 03/L-209) whose bill files are not on the current register — i.e., for building the historical baseline of how long Kosovo banking bills take from first reading to gazette.

source_name: Instituti GAP — analyses of Kosovo's legislative strategy and process
why_relevant: Independent think tank that audits how well the Government's legislative programme is actually executed (slippage rates, bills dropped, consultation quality). Useful as a calibration layer: it tells you how much to discount announced legislative timelines when forecasting when a banking/payments bill will really reach the gazette.

source_name: Kallxo.com — legislative-process journalism (draft-law analyses)
why_relevant: Investigative outlet that produces article-by-article analyses of pending Kosovo draft laws, including digital/financial-adjacent bills (e.g. digital signatures and seals — directly relevant to payments authentication). Useful as an early-warning pointer to bills before they surface prominently on institutional sites, and for identifying contested provisions.

source_name: KoSSev — bilingual (sq/sr) coverage of Kosovo government and Assembly decisions
why_relevant: One of the few outlets covering Kosovo institutional decisions in Serbian alongside Albanian, including government approval of budgets and international financial agreements. Provides sr-language naming of bills and decisions, which helps resolve the same act across the sq/sr official texts.

source_name: Njësia për Inteligjencë Financiare e Kosovës (NJIF-K / FIU-K) — official site
why_relevant: The FIU is the primary AML/CFT rule-setter and supervisor-of-reporting outside the central bank. Site is trilingual (sq/en/sr) and carries legislation, administrative instructions, sanctions lists, the goAML reporting gateway, publications and news — the anchor source for this cell.

source_name: NJIF-K Legjislacioni — laws, administrative instructions, international standards
why_relevant: Single page aggregating the binding rule stack for reporting entities: Law 05/L-096 (AML/CFT), Law 08/L-146 (international financial sanctions), Law 08/L-265 (beneficial owners registry), 15+ udhëzime administrative 2013–2025 (beneficial owner, NPOs, legal professionals, online activity), plus CoE/EU/UN instruments. Administrative instructions are where filing thresholds and deadlines actually live.

source_name: NJIF-K Sanctions Lists page (Listat e sanksioneve)
why_relevant: Publishes four consolidated designation lists that Kosovo reporting entities must screen against: FIU-K national list (XLSX), UN Security Council list (PDF), EU list (PDF), and OFAC list (XLSX). Update cadence is visibly uneven (UN dated Aug 2026, EU Apr 2026, FIU-K and OFAC Jun 2024), which is itself a trackable signal about national list staleness.

source_name: NJIF-K goAML electronic reporting gateway (report.fic-ks.org)
why_relevant: Confirms Kosovo runs UNODC goAML as the single filing channel for reporting entities. Registration notices, schema/XSD version changes and onboarding deadlines announced here are hard operational deadlines for banks and PSPs. The gateway itself is at report.fic-ks.org/GOAML/ (login-walled).

source_name: NJIF-K Publications — annual reports, typologies, indicators, statistics, high-risk country lists
why_relevant: Annual reports (e.g. Raporti Vjetor) give STR/CTR volumes, dissemination counts and supervisory/sanctioning activity; typologies and 'indicators' documents are effectively soft rules banks are expected to build detection scenarios against. High-risk third-country lists drive enhanced due diligence obligations.

source_name: Draft law amending Law No. 05/L-096 on AML/CFT (Projektligji, Office of the Prime Minister)
why_relevant: A live 2026 amendment to the core AML/CFT law — the single highest-value forward-looking regulatory signal in this cell. Government-approved draft text published on the PM's office site indicates changes to obligations, thresholds and possibly filing deadlines before they hit the gazette.

source_name: Council of Europe PECK / PECK II — Kosovo* AML/CFT compliance assessment and follow-up reports (rm.coe.int)
why_relevant: Kosovo is NOT a MONEYVAL member; its FATF-standard evaluation is delivered through the CoE/EU joint 'Project against Economic Crime in Kosovo' (PECK/PECK II) using MONEYVAL methodology. These assessment and follow-up reports produce the recommendations and action-plan dates that become de-facto national AML deadlines. Available in both en and sq.

source_name: MONEYVAL (Council of Europe) — plenary outcomes, methodology, FIU pages
why_relevant: Even though Kosovo is not evaluated as a MONEYVAL member, MONEYVAL sets the methodology, publishes the regional plenary outcomes and typologies that shape Kosovo's assessments, and its regional peers' MERs (AL, ME, RS, MK, BA) are the benchmark Kosovo supervisors are compared against.

source_name: Banka Qendrore e Republikës së Kosovës — Rregullore për parandalimin e pastrimit të parave (AML regulation for licensed institutions)
why_relevant: The AML rulebook is split: the FIU issues udhëzime for all reporting entities, while the CBK issues the binding prudential regulation for licensed banks/MFIs/PSPs (including the newer regulation on information accompanying transfers of funds and crypto-asset transfers). Boundary source for this cell — needed to know which deadline comes from which publisher. Available in sq, sr and en.
